'''Raúl Albiol Tortajada''' (born 4 September 1985) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central defender]].

He spent most of his career with [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], winning five major titles between the first two teams and the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League]] with the third. He amassed [[La Liga]] totals of 394 matches and eight goals over 16 seasons, and also played several years in [[Serie A]] with [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]].

A [[Spain national football team|Spain international]] since 2007, Albiol represented the country in two [[FIFA World Cup|World Cups]] and as many [[UEFA European Championship|European Championships]], winning three tournaments including the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Valencia===
Born in [[Vilamarxant]], [[Valencian Community]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/villarreal/2021/09/14/613f6eb7e2704ef6498b45c9.html|title=Albiol, experiencia en Champions al servicio del Villarreal|trans-title=Albiol, Champions experience at the service of Villarreal|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Víctor|last=Franch|language=es|date=14 September 2021|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref> Albiol started playing football with two modest clubs in his native region, moving to local giants [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] before celebrating his 10th birthday. He made his first-team debut on 24 September 2003 in a [[UEFA Cup]] [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|first-round tie]] against [[AIK Fotboll|AIK]] at 18 years and 20 days,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/es/news/27/laliga-santander/2009/06/25/1346075/los-perfiles-de-goalcom-ra%C3%BAl-albiol|title=Los perfiles de Goal.com: Raúl Albiol|trans-title=Goal.com's profiles: Raúl Albiol|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Francisco|last=Ortí|language=es|date=25 June 2009|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref><ref name=UEFA>{{cite web|url=https://es.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0195-0e6a710a1702-83b8f95fc9ea-1000--el-valencia-toma-la-iniciativa/|title=El Valencia toma la iniciativa|trans-title=Valencia take initiative|publisher=UEFA|language=es|date=25 September 2003|access-date=9 March 2014}}</ref> but spent the first year still registered with [[Valencia CF Mestalla|the reserves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-albiol-ultima-perla-defensiva-cantera-valencia-20090625123153.html|title=Albiol, la última 'perla' defensiva de la cantera del Valencia|trans-title=Albiol, the last defensive 'gem' of Valencia's youth system|publisher=[[Europa Press]]|language=es|date=25 June 2009|access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref>

In August 2004, whilst travelling to sign a deal to join [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on [[Loan (association football)|loan]], Albiol was involved in a serious car accident, being put in [[intensive care]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/01/12/futbol/1105565585.html|title=Albiol reaparece tras su accidente|trans-title=Albiol reappears after accident|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=12 January 2005|access-date=13 April 2009}}</ref> He managed to recover completely and, after reappearing in January, played an important role in the team [[2004–05 La Liga|surviving the relegation battle]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2005/01/23/actualidad/1106468517_850215.html|title=El Getafe saca petróleo de tres jugadas|trans-title=Getafe drill for oil in three plays|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=23 January 2005|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.libertaddigital.com/deportes/el-getafe-confirma-su-permanencia-en-primera-tras-ganar-por-la-minima-al-albacete-1276248685/|title=El Getafe confirma su permanencia en Primera tras ganar por la mínima al Albacete|trans-title=Getafe confirm survival in ''Primera'' after beating Albacete by the odd goal|newspaper=[[Libertad Digital]]|language=es|date=10 April 2005|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span05.html|title=Spain 2004/05|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first1=Jorge|last1=Santos|first2=Ángel David|last2=Martínez|first3=Daniel|last3=Dalence|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref> He made his [[La Liga]] debut on 15 January 2005 in a 1–1 home draw with [[Atlético Madrid]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/01/15/liga/1105814577.html|title=El Getafe paraliza a un Atlético inefable|trans-title=Getafe paralyse unheard-of Atlético|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Fernando|last=Llamas|language=es|date=16 January 2005|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> and scored against another side from the capital, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], in a 2–1 home win two months later.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/03/13/liga/1110735959.html|title=Getafe, otra tumba para el Real Madrid|trans-title=Getafe, another grave for Real Madrid|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Fernando|last=Llamas|language=es|date=15 March 2005|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref>

Albiol returned to the [[Mestalla Stadium]] the [[2005–06 La Liga|following season]], and quickly established himself as first-choice due to his versatility.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/albumes/2009/06/10/mercado_fichajes/index_6.html|title=Los 25 jugadores más deseados de Europa|trans-title=The 25 most-wanted players in Europe|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=10 June 2009|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://espanol.eurosport.com/futbol/liga/2012-2013/albiol-clave-en-el-madrid_sto3398169/story.shtml|title=Albiol, clave en el Madrid|trans-title=Albiol, key at Madrid|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|language=es|date=25 August 2012|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref> In the opening game of [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]], he scored the winner against [[Real Betis]] in a 2–1 home victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/203769/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Valencia 2–1 Real Betis|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=26 August 2006|access-date=12 November 2012}}</ref> He also scored from long distance against [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] on 12 September 2006 in the [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League|group stage]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]], which Valencia won 4–2 away.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01b9-0ea876f8b8f3-358dd046365d-1000--olympiacos-undone-by-magic-morientes/|title=Olympiacos undone by magic Morientes|publisher=UEFA|first=Graham|last=Wood|date=12 September 2006|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref>

During his four-season spell with the first team, Albiol played at least 29 league games, and he helped to victory in the [[2007–08 Copa del Rey|2007–08 edition]] of the [[Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=684523.html|title=Cup triumph salvages Valencia's season|publisher=UEFA|date=17 April 2008|access-date=8 August 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024030752/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=684523.html|archive-date=24 October 2012}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:RAlbiol.JPG|thumb|upright|Albiol playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2009]]
On 25 June 2009, Albiol joined Real Madrid for a fee thought to be in the region of €15&nbsp;million,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/5634990/Real-Madrid-sign-Raul-Albiol-and-step-up-Karim-Benzema-chase.html|title=Real Madrid sign Raul Albiol and step up Karim Benzema chase|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=25 June 2009|access-date=25 June 2009}}</ref> becoming the first Spanish player signed by [[Florentino Pérez]] upon his return to the presidency.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/espanhol/0,,MUL1216875-9845,00-DIRETOR+DO+REAL+MADRID+DESCARTA+VILLA+E+DIZ+QUE+ESPANHOIS+SERAO+CONTRATADOS.html|title=Diretor do Real Madrid descarta Villa e diz que espanhóis serão contratados|trans-title=Real Madrid director discards Villa and says Spaniards will be signed|publisher=[[TV Globo|Globo Esporte]]|language=pt|date=3 July 2009|access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref> He scored his first goal on 8 December in a 3–1 [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] win away to [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01e0-0e738137130e-2ca7e102c35b-1000--madrid-march-on-as-marseille-miss-out/|title=Madrid march on as Marseille miss out|publisher=UEFA|first=Chris|last=Burke|date=8 December 2009|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> He was an undisputed starter during [[2009–10 La Liga|the league campaign]], mainly due to [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]]'s serious knee injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/1211284-grave-lesion-de-pepe-se-pierde-el-resto-de-la-temporada|title=Grave lesión de Pepe: se pierde el resto de la temporada|trans-title=Serious Pepe injury: he misses rest of season|newspaper=[[La Nación]]|language=es|date=13 December 2009|access-date=8 August 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200819061518/https://www.lanacion.com.ar/deportes/futbol/grave-lesion-de-pepe-se-pierde-el-resto-de-la-temporada-nid1211284/|archive-date=19 August 2020}}</ref>

In the [[2010–11 Real Madrid CF season|2010–11 season]], Albiol was relegated to the bench as Real brought in another player for his position, [[Ricardo Carvalho]], only appearing in the league through injury or suspension to teammates;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.es/20120204/deportes-futbol/abci-albiol2012-201202041301.html|title=Albiol, el último de la fila|trans-title=Albiol, last in line|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|first=Tomás|last=González|language=es|date=4 February 2012|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.libertaddigital.com/deportes/2012-05-11/mallorca-ultimo-tren-para-albiol-1276458266/|title=Mallorca, último tren para Albiol|trans-title=Mallorca, last train for Albiol|newspaper=Libertad Digital|language=es|date=11 May 2012|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> he did start, however, in the club's [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|domestic cup run]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/02/06/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1328523225.html|title=Albiol, contra las cuerdas|trans-title=Albiol, against the ropes|newspaper=Marca|first1=Hugo|last1=Cerezo|first2=Miguel Ángel|last2=Lara|language=es|date=6 February 2012|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref> On 26 January 2011, in the semi-final first leg against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] (1–0 away victory), he cleared a [[Luís Fabiano]] shot just before it crossed the goal line.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/312248?cc=5739|title=Benzema advantage|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=26 January 2011|access-date=3 February 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525152545/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/312248?cc=5739|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref> On 16 April, he was [[Sent off (association football)|sent off]] for [[Foul (association football)|fouling]] former Valencia teammate [[David Villa]] inside the [[penalty area]] during [[El Clásico]] with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], which resulted in the first goal in a 1–1 league home draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301944?cc=5739|title=Ronaldo earns draw in ''el clasico''|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=16 April 2011|access-date=20 April 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525152545/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301944?cc=5739|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref>

On 6 August 2012, Albiol renewed his contract until June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330112565763/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_Announcement_2012-08-06.htm|title=Official announcement|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=6 August 2012|access-date=6 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120808202308/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330112565763/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_Announcement_2012-08-06.htm|archive-date=8 August 2012}}</ref> On 27 November, in his first appearance as [[Captain (association football)|captain]], at home against [[CD Alcoyano|Alcoyano]] in the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup]], he had to be stretchered off after only one minute, being sidelined for approximately one month with an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/11/27/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1354049866.html|title=Albiol, de tres a cuatro semanas de baja|trans-title=Albiol, three to four weeks out|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=27 November 2012|access-date=28 November 2012}}</ref>

===Napoli===
On 21 July 2013, Albiol joined [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] for a reported €12&nbsp;million,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football-napoli-sign-spain-defender-raul-albiol-from-real-madrid-deal-is-for-four-years|title=Football: Napoli sign Spain defender Raul Albiol from Real Madrid; deal is for four years|newspaper=[[The Straits Times]]|date=21 July 2013|access-date=4 July 2019}}</ref> signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.sscnapoli.it/static/news/Il-Napoli-ufficializza-l-acquisto-di-Raul-Albiol-600.aspx|title=Il Napoli ufficializza l'acquisto di Raul Albiol|trans-title=Napoli make signing of Raul Albiol official|publisher=S.S.C. Napoli|language=it|date=21 July 2013|access-date=21 July 2013}}</ref> He made his [[Serie A]] debut on 25 August, in a 3–0 home win over [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Napoli/25-08-2013/napoli-bologna-diretta-campionato-calcio-seriea-prima-giornata-201031849154.shtml|title=Napoli-Bologna 3–0: apre Callejon, poi la doppietta di super Hamsik|trans-title=Napoli-Bologna 3–0: Callejon starts it, then double by super Hamsik|newspaper=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|first=Gennaro|last=Bozza|language=it|date=25 August 2013|access-date=11 December 2013}}</ref>

Albiol scored his first goal for the [[Rafael Benítez]]-led team on 25 January 2014, with an 88th-minute equaliser in a 1–1 home draw against [[AC ChievoVerona|ChievoVerona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/306630/report|title=Napoli held at home|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=25 January 2014|access-date=7 September 2014}}</ref> On 3 May, he played the entire [[2014 Coppa Italia final|final]] of the [[Coppa Italia]], helping to a 3–1 defeat of [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref name=COPPA>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/130949/fiorentina-vs-napoli/report|title=Fiorentina 1–3 Napoli: Partenopei come out on top in Coppa Italia final|publisher=Goal|date=3 May 2014|access-date=7 May 2014}}</ref>

===Villarreal===
On 4 July 2019, the 33-year-old Albiol returned to Spain after agreeing to a three-year deal with [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.villarrealcf.es/en/news/item/24770-welcome-raul-albiol|title=Welcome, Raúl Albiol!|publisher=Villarreal CF|date=4 July 2019|access-date=4 July 2019}}</ref> He made his debut on 17 August, in a 4–4 home draw with [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/cronica/2019/08/18/5d5885deca4741365e8b45aa.html|title=Villarreal and Granada draw in eight-goal thriller|newspaper=Marca|first=Henry|last=Flynn|date=18 August 2019|access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref>

Albiol scored twice from 11 appearances in the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League]], as the club won the first major honour of its 98-year history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pt.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0264-1102679f1685-dcb518fd71d4-1000--final-de-la-europa-league-villarreal-manchester-united/|title=Finalista de la Europa League: Villarreal|trans-title=Europa League finalists: Villarreal|publisher=UEFA|language=es|date=24 May 2021|access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref><ref name=EL>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57224112|title=Villarreal 1–1 Manchester United|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Simon|last=Stone|date=26 May 2021|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> In the [[2021 UEFA Super Cup]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], he missed the decisive [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] in [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|the shoot-out]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58157867|title=Chelsea 1–1 Villarreal (Chelsea win 6–5 on penalties)|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Mark|last=Sterling|date=11 August 2021|access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref>

On 12 April 2022, Albiol was named [[player of the match]] in a 1–1 away draw against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|Champions League quarter-finals second leg]], securing Villarreal's qualification by winning 2–1 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0274-14e4c515c083-62007a25cd48-1000--bayern-1-1-villarreal-agg-1-2-last-gasp-chukwueze-sends-/|title=Bayern 1–1 Villarreal (agg 1–2): Last-gasp Chukwueze sends Spanish side through to semi-finals|publisher=UEFA|date=12 April 2022|access-date=8 September 2024}}</ref> In May 2025, four months shy of his 40th birthday, he left the [[La Cerámica Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/futbol/villarreal-cf/20250526/raul-albiol-niega-retirada-quiero-seguir-jugando_300675517.html|title=Raúl Albiol se resiste a la retirada y busca equipo: "Mi mujer me mata pero quiero seguir jugando"|trans-title=Raúl Albiol just will not retire and looks for a team: "My wife will kill me but I want to continue playing"|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=26 May 2025|access-date=11 June 2025}}</ref>

===Pisa===
Albiol returned to Italy and its top tier in September 2025, joining newly-promoted [[Pisa SC|Pisa]] as a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pisasportingclub.com/en/raul-albiol-is-a-pisa-sc-player/|title=Raul Albiol is a Pisa SC player!|publisher=Pisa SC|date=2 September 2025|access-date=2 September 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Raúl Albiol 2009.jpg|thumb|upright|Albiol lining up for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in 2009]]
Having represented [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain at under-21 level]], Albiol made his debut for the [[Spain national football team|senior squad]] on 13 October 2007 in an [[UEFA Euro 2008]] [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|qualifier]] against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], a 3–1 away win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/289897/0/victoria/seleccion/dinamarca/|title=España sale del túnel tras su triunfo en Dinamarca (1–3)|trans-title=Spain exit tunnel after win in Denmark (1–3)|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=13 October 2007|access-date=28 December 2015}}</ref> In the final stages, he appeared twice for the eventual champions, against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] ([[Substitute (association football)|subbing]] in for the injured [[Carles Puyol]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2008/7363455.stm|title=Sweden 1–2 Spain|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Chris|last=Bevan|date=14 June 2008|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref> and [[Greece national football team|Greece]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/euro_2008/7363473.stm|title=Russia 2–0 Sweden & Greece 1–2 Spain|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Andrew|last=McKenzie|date=18 June 2008|access-date=28 December 2015}}</ref>

New national team coach [[Vicente del Bosque]] included Albiol in the squad for the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/deportes-futbol-espaa-seleccion-idLTASIE5500K320090601|title=FUTBOL-España, con Iniesta y Piqué en Confederaciones|trans-title=FOOTBALL-Spain, with Iniesta and Piqué in the Confederations|publisher=[[Reuters]]|first=Mark|last=Elkington|language=es|date=1 June 2009|access-date=21 November 2021}}</ref> He started in Spain's first game, partnering Puyol in central defence ahead of Valencia teammate [[Carlos Marchena]] and helping defeat [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]] 5–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/news/y=2009/m=6/news=roja-lean-the-left-1072428.html|title=La Roja lean to the left|publisher=FIFA|date=16 June 2009|access-date=18 April 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160804081845/http://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/news/y=2009/m=6/news=roja-lean-the-left-1072428.html|archive-date=4 August 2016}}</ref>

Albiol was picked for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], but did not leave the bench for the eventual champions after having suffered an injury in training.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://spain.worldcupblog.org/world-cup-2010/breaking-ouch-news-raul-albiol-injured.html|title=Breaking (ouch!) news: Raúl Albiol injured|publisher=World Cup Blog|first=Ade|last=C.|date=26 June 2010|access-date=3 July 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101124231841/http://spain.worldcupblog.org/world-cup-2010/breaking-ouch-news-raul-albiol-injured.html|archive-date=24 November 2010}}</ref> Again as an unused player, he was also in the squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]] tournament in Poland and Ukraine, which also ended in victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/abci-secundarios-espanoles-eurocopa-201207020000_noticia.html|title=Reina, Valdés, Juanfran, Albiol y Llorente: los otros campeones de la Eurocopa|trans-title=Reina, Valdés, Juanfran, Albiol and Llorente: the other Eurocup champions|newspaper=ABC|language=es|date=2 July 2012|access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref>

Albiol was named in Spain's 23-man squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27647635|title=World Cup 2014: Spain drop Alvaro Negredo and Jesus Navas|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 May 2014|access-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> He made his debut in a major finals in the last group match against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] with the Spanish already eliminated, playing the whole 90 minutes alongside [[Sergio Ramos]] in central defence in a 3–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285263|title=Australia 0–3 Spain|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Saj|last=Chowdhury|date=23 June 2014|access-date=24 June 2014}}</ref>

On 11 October 2018, after taking part in the 4–1 [[Exhibition game#International football|friendly]] away victory over [[Wales national football team|Wales]], Albiol appeared in his 52nd international to become the most-[[Cap (sport)|capped]] player from his region of birth, surpassing [[David Albelda]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/report?gameId=510031|title=Paco Alcacer scores twice as dominant Spain demolish Wales in Cardiff|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=11 October 2018|access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://rfef.es/es/raul-albiol-se-convierte-valenciano-mas-partidos-como-internacional|title=Raúl Albiol se convierte el valenciano con más partidos como internacional|trans-title=Raúl Albiol becomes the Valencian player with the most international appearances|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|language=es|date=13 October 2018|access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref> He went on to total 58 appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0274-14fdb4090c44-d5a977fb37af-1000--villarreal-captain-raul-albiol-on-beating-bayern-facing-/|title=Villarreal captain Raúl Albiol on beating Bayern, facing Liverpool, video games and making history|publisher=UEFA|date=27 April 2022|access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A physically strong player who excels in the air, Albiol's main asset is his versatility, as he can play as a [[centre-back]], [[right-back]] or [[defensive midfielder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.areanapoli.it/squadra/raul_albiol.html|title=Raul Albiol|publisher=Area Napoli|first=Luca|last=Ruggiero|language=it|access-date=1 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/soccer/a-closer-look-at-spains-euro-2012-squad/article4235828/|title=A closer look at Spain's Euro 2012 squad|newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=6 June 2012|access-date=17 May 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Albiol's nickname is "''El Chori''".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/futbol-nos-vemos-fuerza-superar/20100106dasdaiftb_23/Tes|title=Nos vemos con fuerza para superar al Barça|trans-title=We can see ourselves beating Barça|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Marco|last=Ruiz|language=es|date=6 January 2010|access-date=16 May 2012}}</ref> His older brother [[Miguel Albiol|Miguel]] was also a footballer, while his father, also named Miguel, appeared in the [[Segunda División]] for [[CE Sabadell FC|Sabadell]]. The youngest sibling, Brian, was named after [[Brian Laudrup]], whom Raúl admired on account of his success with the Denmark national team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.levante-emv.com/deportes/2010/07/13/vilamarxant-emociona-albiol/722348.html|title=Vilamarxant se emociona con Albiol|trans-title=Vilamarxant gets emotional with Albiol|newspaper=[[Levante-EMV]]|first=R.|last=Montaner|language=es|date=13 July 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2010/10/26/mas_futbol/1288074418_850215.html|title=Los hermanos Albiol frente a frente|trans-title=The Albiol brothers face to face|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=26 October 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330072821710/noticia/Entrevista/1330072821710.htm?idEsp=1330065768332|title=RealAlbiol: "Mourinho nos ha dado carácter. Día a día demuestra lo gran entrenador que es"|trans-title=RealAlbiol: "Mourinho has built our character. Every day he shows the great manager he is"|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=17 November 2011|access-date=27 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120908023717/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330072821710/noticia/Entrevista/1330072821710.htm?idEsp=1330065768332|archive-date=8 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lasprovincias.es/deportes/futbol/albiol-capitanes-20201008185505-nt.html|title=Albiol: "Ya no habrá capitanes como los de antes"|trans-title=Albiol: "Captains will never be what they used to be"|newspaper=[[Las Provincias]]|first=Cayetano|last=Ros|language=es|date=8 October 2020|access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref>

Albiol fathered two daughters with his wife Alicia.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elpais.com/articulo/deportes/Acuerdo/Valencia/Madrid/Albiol/elpepidep/20090625elpepidep_3/Tes?print=1|title=Acuerdo entre el Valencia y el Madrid por Albiol|trans-title=Agreement between Valencia and Madrid for Albiol|newspaper=El País|first1=Diego|last1=Torres|first2=Nadia|last2=Tronchoni|language=es|date=25 June 2009|access-date=15 July 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lasprovincias.es/20100109/deportes/valencia/alma-valenciana-albiol-20100109.html|title=El 'alma' valenciana de Albiol|trans-title=Albiol's Valencia 'soul' (Alma in English)|newspaper=Las Provincias|first=Toni|last=Calero|language=es|date=9 January 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> In 2008, with [[Guillermo Franco]] and [[Marcos Senna]], he founded Evangélico FC, an organisation consisting of 140 athletes and 16 coaches which sought to promote Christian values among young athletes in Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://protestantedigital.com/ciudades/22149/Marcos_Senna_presento_el_Evangelico_FC_equipo_de_futbol_inspirado_en_los_valores_cristianos|title=Marcos Senna presentó el Evangélico FC, equipo de fútbol inspirado en los valores cristianos|trans-title=Marcos Senna presented Evangélico FC, football team inspired by Christian values|publisher=Protestante Digital|language=es|date=20 October 2008|access-date=18 January 2019}}</ref>
